A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same pPE study. The main text, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material and reordered heatmaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-training experiments, benchmark accuracies, training trajectories, response lengths, and behavioral analyses, including generalization experiments in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds results for an RFT model trained without prior prompts.

M1.justification: The five proposed pPE approaches, prompt templates, GRPO procedure, and accuracy-plus-format rewards remain unchanged. No PP is an added experimental control, not a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions train on STILLv3 and evaluate AIME2024, AMC12 ’22–’23, MATH-500, HumanEval+, and GPQA-Diamond. No PP uses this existing coverage; no dataset, domain, or task scenario is added.

E2.justification: v2 adds one comparator: Qwen2.5-7B trained with RFT without prior prompts, labeled No PP. It participates in accuracy, response-length, training-dynamics, and behavioral comparisons. Existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: The new No PP control removes prior-prompt instructions and the format reward, using an accuracy reward capped at 1.0 (Section 3.2). Existing experiments retain their stated splits, budgets, metrics, and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: v2 adds a joint prior-prompt/format-reward removal analysis, examining its effects on performance, training trajectories, verbosity, and behavioral patterns (Figures 4–7). Existing generalization analyses and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix D.4.1 still specifies evaluation once with a fixed random seed. Neither version reports confidence intervals, repeated-run variability, or significance tests; v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained. New No PP results include 26.67% AIME accuracy, 70.40% MATH accuracy, 45.41% average accuracy, and 1,569.87 average response tokens, alongside training curves and behavioral counts (Tables 1–2, 5, 7, and 9).

T1.justification: No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or theoretical derivation is added or revised. Mathematical expressions in the retained prompts and qualitative examples are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: five iPE-inspired pPE approaches shape model behavior, pPE outperforms corresponding iPE baselines, and null-example pPE achieves the highest average performance.

C2.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 now attribute some gains and behaviors to math-only RFT and distinguish the effect of including prior prompts from differences among the five prompt types. v2 also explains the base-model choice and explicitly qualifies the behavioral analyses as preliminary, with mechanisms beyond scope.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 documents the new control's omitted instructions and format reward and its accuracy-reward scaling. Existing library versions, training script, hardware disclosure, evaluation details, and classifier prompts in Appendix D remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and Appendix A related-work discussion are retained. The paper remains positioned as investigating an understudied RFT component through established inference-time prompting strategies.

P1.justification: The introduction, experimental rationale, and results discussion receive localized rewrites and expanded explanations, including a clearer iPE definition. The section hierarchy, conclusion, and most appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 1, 2, 5, 7, and 9 gain No PP rows, and Figures 4–7 gain corresponding plotted entries. Heatmaps in Figures 7 and 34–36 reorder categories without changing existing values. Captions and figure/table placement also change.

improvement.justification: The No PP control provides useful evidence about gains and behaviors arising without prior prompts, and the preliminary-analysis caveat improves qualification. Benefits are limited because the control also changes the reward. v2 also introduces incorrect comparisons: No PP's 70.40 MATH score does not exceed Think's 73.20, and Knowledge ties No PP at 37.35 on AMC, contrary to Section 4.1. Despite these errors, the added control makes the empirical comparison modestly more informative.
